name: llama-cpp-cpu-variants
description: ggml's GGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS runtime multi-versioning: the repack::gemm/gemv templated matmul kernels that back llama.cpp's per-ISA-tier dispatch libraries (libggml-cpu-armv8.0_1.so ... libggml-cpu-armv9.2_2.so), independent of KleidiAI.
why_it_matters: A GGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS release ships several libggml-cpu-<isa-tier>.{so,dylib} files and picks one at runtime based on detected CPU features -- if that selection silently picks a lower ISA tier than the CPU actually supports, you get correct output at a needless speed penalty, with nothing in a normal run to say so. This is a DIFFERENT dispatch question from llama-cpp-kleidiai: KleidiAI is one optional accelerator; the repack path is ggml's own baseline multi-ISA matmul dispatch, present (and REPACK=1 in system_info) even when KleidiAI is off.

l1.note: Itanium-mangled C++ template symbols (ggml::cpu::repack::gemm<...>/gemv<...>), one instantiation per quant block type. The leading '_?' is deliberate and platform-load-bearing: verify_dispatch.py's Darwin nm path strips ALL leading underscores (Mach-O's own linker-decoration underscore plus the one Itanium mangling already starts with), leaving 'ZN4ggml...'; the Linux nm path does not strip, leaving '_ZN4ggml...'. A regex anchored to only one form silently matches 0 symbols on the other platform -- verified by running the SAME regex against both a real Darwin dylib and a real Linux .so (see verified_against).

l2.note: No per-symbol 'kleidiai: primary kernel feature X'-style selection line exists for the repack dispatcher, so this target has NO advertised_family: the system_info line is compile-time-of-the-loaded-variant ISA flags (REPACK/DOTPROD/I8MM/SVE/SVE2/...), useful context but not a per-kernel claim to check L3 against. Verdicts for this target are therefore always an *_EXECUTED_NO_ADVERTISED_FEATURE / NO_DISPATCH_OBSERVED shape (informational: 'did the repack path run at all'), never a MISMATCH/DISPATCHED shape. 'load_backend_cpu' only fires on ggml builds using GGML_BACKEND_DL (dynamic backend loading, e.g. Homebrew's whisper-cpp formula) -- most llama.cpp release/from-source builds link the CPU backend statically and never print this line; it is included for the (untested here) case a caller points this preset at a GGML_BACKEND_DL build of llama.cpp.

l3.note: Same fail-closed breakpoint mechanism as llama-cpp-kleidiai. See caveats: on the one artifact this could actually be executed against (a from-source build with KleidiAI compiled in), the repack path resolves 32 real candidate symbols but was observed to dispatch 0 of them for every workload tried -- KleidiAI's buffer-type negotiation appears to win for every tensor this model has, so the repack fallback path this target targets never got exercised. That is a genuine, reproducible result, not a probe failure (candidate symbols DO resolve; see verified_against) -- but it means the 'these ARE the kernels used when the ISA-tier selection falls back' half of this target's claim remains unconfirmed pending a KleidiAI-free build or a model/quant combination that forces the repack path.

workload.note: Same argv shape as llama-cpp-kleidiai -- any llama-cli build accepts it.

verified_against.platform: darwin-arm64 (Apple M4 Max), scanning a linux/aarch64 artifact
verified_against.artifact: official llama.cpp b10276 ubuntu-arm64 release tarball, all 8 libggml-cpu-{armv8.0_1,armv8.2_1,armv8.2_2,armv8.2_3,armv8.6_1,armv8.6_2,armv9.2_1,armv9.2_2}.so files
verified_against.result: Each of the 8 variant .so files: 0 kai_ symbols; the dispatch_regex above matches exactly 32 symbols (16 gemm + 16 gemv instantiations) via `polygraph check --level 1` (which counts ALL nm-listed entries, defined+undefined, as the denominator -- 577 there; a stricter defined-function-only count via `nm -D ... | grep -c ' T '` separately gave 393) -- identical across all 8 variants (they differ in compiled ISA target, not in which symbols they export). Confirms both halves of this preset's binary_globs/lib_globs claim (GGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS really does ship 8 separate libs in the official Linux arm64 release) and that the regex's Linux ('_ZN...') symbol form is correct.

L1: 32/673 symbols match (16 gemm + 16 gemv), confirming the regex's Darwin ('ZN...', both underscores stripped) symbol form is also correct. L2: system_info line captured with REPACK = 1 present. L3: 32 candidate symbols resolve real breakpoints (probe correctly instrumented, not silently uninstrumented) but total_hits = 0 across both a short decode workload (t=2, n=4) and a longer prefill+decode workload (380-word prompt, t=8, n=8) -- see l3.note above for why this is reported as an open question, not a pass.

caveats: L3's positive-dispatch claim ('the repack kernels are what actually runs when ISA-tier selection matters') is UNCONFIRMED on the only artifact available to test end-to-end here, because that artifact also has KleidiAI compiled in and KleidiAI's buffer-type negotiation appears to claim every tensor this model has before the repack path is ever tried. A KleidiAI-free build (e.g. the official release binaries, which have 0 kai_ symbols) would be a cleaner test of this specific claim, but those are Linux ELF binaries this macOS host cannot execute.
No advertised_family exists for this target (see l2.note) -- exit code will be 2 (undetermined) even on a fully successful run; that is by design, not a bug.
